m2.title: Per-unit failure isolation (load-bearing)
m2.imperative: In run_grip_batch, wrap the fit_fn call in try/except: on any exception, build an error record via record_fn (error_record) with a session_id sentinel (fit_fn raised before a real session_id was resolved) and the exception message, store.upsert it, increment counts['errors'], and CONTINUE to the next session -- one bad session must never abort the batch. Write the load-bearing test: inject a fit_fn that raises for exactly ONE (gp, session_type) among several, assert the batch continues, the failing session lands in the store as fit_status='error' with the exception message, and every other session still gets fitted.

postconditions.statement: one failing session is isolated: recorded as error, batch continues, other sessions still fitted

constraints: per-unit failure isolation is non-negotiable (repo-wide never-lose-a-failure convention)

m3.title: get_grip_at consumer query surface (additive to grip_store.py)
m3.imperative: Add get_grip_at(store, year, gp_name, session_type, cumulative_track_laps) -> tuple[float, float] to grip_store.py (additive only -- do not touch anything else in that file). Evaluate the stored session's curve (session_offset + curve_asymptote*(1-exp(-curve_rate*x))) at x=cumulative_track_laps for an 'ok' fit; for a thin_fallback record (no curve params) fall back to (session_offset, session_offset_sigma) as a stated simplification. Propagate sigma via a first-order delta-method combination of session_offset_sigma, curve_asymptote_sigma, curve_rate_sigma and the stored curve_offset_correlation cross-term -- never silently imply sigma=0. Define and raise a new named exception (e.g. GripRecordNotFoundError) when (year, gp_name, session_type) has no stored record, or the stored record has no usable fit (error status / session_offset is None) -- never a bare KeyError. Write tests covering: normal-fit curve evaluation, thin-fallback simplified path, and the named-exception raise on a missing/unusable record.

postconditions.statement: get_grip_at correctly evaluates the curve, returns (mu, sigma) with honest sigma, and raises the named exception on a missing/unusable record
